title: Governing and Scaling Agents in Heterogeneous Environments
tldr: Antonio Ojea and Tomás Tormo present Agent Mesh, a network for agents running on Kubernetes, laptops, VMs and serverless, built on a libp2p peer-to-peer data plane with Kademlia discovery. Policy travels with each node as signed, attenuable Biscuit tokens minted at enrollment, and a live hospital demo shows label-based rules keeping EU data in the EU.

key_points.text: Regulated customers run agents on laptops, VMs and serverless as well as Kubernetes, and cannot replace existing platforms, so a Kubernetes-only answer creates silos.
The solution must run as an SDK, a sidecar or a gateway and work with existing open protocols.
A VPN does not fit: it gives L3/L4 connectivity with IPAM pain and no visibility, and a compromised agent gets open access.
Agent traffic falls into five kinds: LLM calls, tools over MCP, agent-to-agent (A2A), external apps such as GitHub, and services the agent exposes.
Data plane: libp2p over a Kademlia DHT, with a cryptographic identity per node, TLS between nodes and built-in service discovery.
Policy: webhooks and Lua/Wasm extensions are opaque and fragile, so they chose Biscuit, signed tokens with a Datalog policy language, exposed to admins through a simpler DSL.
The control plane connects to an external identity provider, compiles policy to Datalog and mints a Biscuit at enrollment. Biscuits work offline, so connected nodes no longer need the control plane.
Biscuit blocks can only attenuate, so a node can narrow delegated rights, for example to one MCP tool or one HTTP path.
Nodes set label requirements for inbound and outbound peers (for example region EU), checked in a five-step exchange before any data flows.
Architecture: control plane, admin-run routers that keep the Kademlia network up, and nodes or embedded SDKs; one binary bundles control plane, router and console.
Demo: the US diagnoser is refused by the laptop's EU-only egress rule, and the model cannot override it because the node enforces it; a banned phone is cut off after the control plane notifies peers.

numbers.text: A new mesh can be created in about 10 seconds using a tunnel broker.
Five categories of agent traffic: LLM, MCP tools, A2A, external apps, exposed services.
A five-step check runs between nodes before any data flows.
Agent Mesh v0.2.0 was just released.

open_gaps.text: Schema-based filtering of MCP traffic is hard to maintain when there can be millions of tools and fields change often.
Region rules depend on admins labeling nodes correctly; the mesh only enforces the labels it is given.
Next: connecting HPC centers and cloud providers to run workflows, with Lawrence Livermore National Lab, and closer work with the A2A protocol.

opportunities.text: Biscuit tokens: offline verification, Datalog policies and attenuation for delegating narrower rights to sub-agents.
Enforce data residency for agent traffic with signed node labels and egress requirements instead of prompt instructions.
Create a mesh or join the public testnet and connect agents across a laptop, a VM and a cluster.
Help with Agent Mesh's A2A integration or new SDK and platform integrations.
